markets.question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 presidential field remains fragmented more than two years out, with no candidate consolidating broad support and top probabilities clustered below 22 percent. JD Vance holds the lead as sitting vice president under a Republican administration, drawing on institutional visibility and early party alignments, while Marco Rubio trails closely as secretary of state amid differing foreign-policy emphases. On the Democratic side, Gavin Newsom, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and Jon Ossoff cluster tightly due to polling shifts, including Ocasio-Cortez’s New Hampshire lead, and the absence of a clear frontrunner. Trader pricing reflects standard midterm headwinds against the incumbent party, with Democrats favored in generic-ballot surveys ahead of November 2026 contests, alongside the finalized early primary calendar beginning in South Carolina. Fundraising, economic conditions, and any post-midterm realignment could widen gaps before formal nominations.
